utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you, Ms. Registrar. This is Thursday, April 3rd, 2008. Welcome the OTP, to representatives, Mr. Seselj, as well as everyone helping us. Today's hearing is going to be devoted to videos, but first there is a small matter we need to solve. Mr. Seselj, yesterday you showed the witness a number of documents coming from -- that were legal documents. You read out a number of excerpts. They were translated, and they are now on the record. And the Judges discussed this amongst themselves and decided that this might be sufficient and that there is no real need for asking for these documents to be tendered, since the documents were translated by the interpreters, and that we have the translation now on the transcript. If you're asking for these documents to be admitted, since they are not translated, we would only be able to give MFI numbers. So what's your position? We need to know what your opinion is. These are documents that you presented during the cross-examination, so it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not tender these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Furthermore, I'm not sure I understood you properly yesterday. I would like you to tell us what you said exactly yesterday. At one point in time yesterday, when talking about the witness, and I will not mention his name, since this is a protected witness, you challenged the truthfulness of what he was saying, and you said he was a false witness. That's your point of view. But you also added something else which was a bit of a problem for me, and I was thinking about it all night, actually, because you said that you intended to publish, on your website or on maybe some other media, the testimony or statement of this witness. So did I misunderstand you or did I understand you properly, because consequences could be huge. As you know, Mr. Seselj, you're a qualified lawyer, so you know, like everyone here, that the statements of protected witnesses are, by definition, also protected, and it is absolutely banned to publish outside this legal arena, these kinds of statements. Maybe I misunderstood you, and I would like to be reassured as to what you intend to do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it is indispensable for you to demand that CLSS compare the recording of the cross-examination of this witness with the text of the transcript. You will then see that I said that no one can declare secret the statement. Aleksandar Gajic gave to me, in which matters are mentioned that concern this witness. Also, I never said I would publish on my website the testimony of the witness who testified yesterday. This was when I opposed moving into private session. I can't repeat everything verbatim, but I remember the purport of what I said. So I ask that you get your interpretation service to compare the interpretation with the transcript. Yesterday, there was some other important matters that remained unsaid. I tried to bring them out in my cross-examination, but I'm not sure I was precise enough, when the witness lied to say that the headquarters of his organisation were on the same premises as the Serbian Chetnik Movement. But you will recall that the witness himself said that the Serbian Chetnik Movement was never registered. When I asked him whether the State gave state offices to such organisations, he confirmed it, but it gives them only to registered ones, not unregistered ones. And I checked and found out that the humanitarian organisation the witness mentioned was never registered. I slept very well last night, but I had to conduct some extra checks, just as the OTP does when I say something, put something forward in this courtroom, and usually they only confirm -- the things they find out only go to confirm what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yesterday, you said something. The Chamber has not conferred on this yet, so I can't say anything as to what the Judges think on this, but I can tell you one thing that's extremely clear and straightforward for everyone here, which is the following: A witness makes a statement under oath, everybody will listen to what the witness is saying, and it's up to everyone, each and every one, to assess whether this witness is telling the truth or not. But to judge on the veracity of this, we can only do this by crossing this with other statements, other documents, other elements. Otherwise, it would be impossible to work as a judge, because we would be asked to draw conclusions when somebody is saying "white" and another witness will be saying "black," and draw conclusions on this, and we'd be supposed to say, maybe, the one who said "black" had lied, but we can't do this. So we cannot have an immediate answer to this kind of request. Yesterday, Mr. Seselj, you said, and I remember it very well, you said, "I'm asking the Judges to sanction this witness, to convict him for false testimony." And you said this just because the witness had said one thing and another witness, for which you had one element, was saying the opposite. But this is not sufficient to draw conclusions at this stage. The conclusions can only be drawn once we have the entire body of evidence, and then we'll be ready to draw conclusions. And if you were in our shoes, you would say exactly the same thing. It's not because someone is saying "white" and the other is saying "black" that you should draw conclusions, final conclusions, without any other elements. Other witnesses will come and they will either confirm or contradict what yesterday's witness said, and you will be -- you will have time to come back to this, and then you can ask us to draw the consequences. But as of today, this is totally impossible. There will be an entire series of witnesses, and we will have plenty of time to assess the body of evidence. That is the whole nature of the contradictory procedure. The whole procedure starts with a trial and ends at the end of a trial. You cannot draw conclusions in the course of the trial. This is not possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted). You will see that the witness later on retracted what he said, and you will see that quite evidently he lied but because there is no trace in the OTP that he had made such a statement. That's why I asked you to take appropriate measures against that witness. Secondly, another problem arises here. I know that in these contradictory proceedings, the rules that apply are mainly those of Anglo-Saxon law. However, even under Anglo-Saxon law, there is an investigation. Your OTP is not conducting investigations at all. They are engaged in passing surveys, in conducting surveys, passing questionnaires around. People, educated and uneducated, make statements, and that's it. It's actually the duty of the Prosecutor to check the statements made by their witnesses before they call them, because the OTP is responsible for everything that fails in this courtroom. We have heard so many fantastic stories here. I've managed to debunk them all, but this is continuing. It's happening again and again. The OTP calls a witness, and the witness produces testimony which is supposed to be true, but then when it's demonstrated that not only is it not true but that 99 per cent of it is false, nothing happens. The witness goes away and the next witness comes. Something like this is impermissible even under Anglo-Saxon law. If the OTP brings four or five witnesses who lie, who make things up, invent things, make false accusations and so on and so forth, and this is demonstrated, then there cannot fail to be measures instituted against the OTP. After these failed expert witnesses, you should have taken certain measures. I'm not an impatient man, I can wait, but certainly, in my opinion, matters have come to a head and the conditions are now in place for you to take measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we take note of this, but now I think my fellow Judge would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, because there was another matter that is still pending from yesterday, and I'm raising it because you, yourself, now raise the issue of contempt proceedings. The issue that was raised yesterday by the Presiding Judge was the issue of interpretation and respect for the Chamber's order for protective measures, because it would seem as if the production of a statement from the gentleman that you contacted, whose name I will not mention here and whose statement we saw yesterday, that statement must have been made under the condition that the gentleman knew that the protected witness was coming here to testify, and the Chamber's order for protective measures for that witness includes, of course, that no one outside the Defence team and the Prosecution team is being informed of the fact that this witness would come to testify. I don't think we ever got an answer from you about this problem yesterday, because it seems as if your Defence team must have revealed to the gentleman who gave the statement to you the facts that the protected witness was going to testify to here, and if that is correct, then that would seem to be in violation of the Chamber's order. I would like you to explain, if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never give confidential documents to anyone for their inspection, apart from the members of my team. However, when preparations are being made for cross-examination, the members of my team are duty-bound to obtain appropriate material for me, and they go in search of that material. I called over your phone and said I learned that this witness participated in a bomb attack on the Belgrade mosque, "Get me from the Belgrade District Court the entire file." And my legal adviser went and got it. And then the people in the court know that we asked for the file of such-and-such a person, but no one told them in the courtroom, "This is a protected witness in these proceedings and that's why we're asking for this." But if you think that absolute protection of protected witnesses is possible, well, it's not. There's always someone who recognises them. Look at what happened yesterday, last night. I got this information 15 minutes ago. I have a mobile telephone number written down here. I don't want to go back into private session or have this redacted from the transcript, so I won't mention the number. If you ask me for it, I'll give it to you right away. But Natasha Kandic rang up Aleksandar Gajic, and she asked him, "Are you looking at our friend? Let's meet, let's have a chat. We have to." And so on and so forth. And he is my Defence witness who previously contacted Natasha Kandic, and we discussed this in open session yesterday. Once Natasha Kandic mentioned the name of a protected witness of the OTP on a TV broadcast. We have the broadcast. I think you received the transcripts of that broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, I think you're beating around the bush. My question to you was if anyone from your team disclosed to Mr. Gajic the fact that the protected witness was coming to testify here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I told you that from the outset. No one from my Defence team disclosed the name of any protected witness called to testify here. However, as soon as this witness began testifying, a certain number of people recognised him, because he was describing his role in the war during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, as the Presiding Judge noticed yesterday, the statement by Mr. Gajic was dated before the person even came here to testify.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why shouldn't it be dated before? Does it say anywhere in the statement that Aleksandar Gajic learned that this man was going to be a protected witness on such-and-such a day? My legal advisors are conducting a investigation, I have a team of investigators, and they discover things on the ground. In a day or two, they'll turn up in front of the house of another witness to take photographs of certain people so that I can check whether these really were the people who appeared in the courtroom or whether the witnesses who came were actors, pretending to be those people. Such suspicions arose in previous trials. If you declare a witness to be protected, does that mean I mustn't say anything to anyone, but I have to grapple with his imagination in the courtroom and then we have to compete to see whose imagination is more vivid? I was never in the places where the witness was. I've never seen the witness before in my life. The witness confirmed that he had never met me, and then what am I supposed to do? He's protected, and I mustn't conduct any sort of investigation to unmask his false statement, to learn about other circumstances impeaching the witness, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If you have concerns about the true identity of a witness, you can raise that in court. There is no way in which you can start this against a protected witness outside the courtroom. The court is the relevant forum in which this issue is to be dealt with, not outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I fully agree with what my fellow Judge has said, but maybe the problem is the following: Your associates are continuing with their investigation. You know, for the trial, you have to prepare for the cross-examination and you also have to prepare for your own witnesses in the future. So I guess that your associates on the field are working, and there's probably some dozens of people working for you, because the lists show they're quite numerous. They're working. Okay. I assume, but I have no element to be sure of this, but I assume that your associates, either when they come to see you or on the phone, tell you and keep you abreast of the development of their work. Maybe this is where there is the problem. Let's imagine that at one point in time one of your associates says, "Okay, Mr. X could be an interesting person. We've contacted him to try and solve this or that problem." You have the list of protected witnesses, and at this point of time, since you know that the witnesses are protected, do you tell your associates, "Watch out, this is a protected witness. You cannot contact him, because he has been granted protective measures. Set him aside"? Or do you tell them, "Continue with your work and contact this witness"? And then this witness could very well tell the OTP, "Mr. Prosecutor, I will agree to be your witness, I have been granted protective measures, and suddenly the accused's associates have called me up, which means that they know that I've been granted protective measures." Have you ever been in this situation, and if so, what was the conduct that you adopted?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were no such situations, but last year, before the identity of all the protected witnesses was disclosed to me, and you know very well that four or five witnesses have not yet been disclosed, before that happened people turned up offering to be witnesses for my Defence. I had no idea that somebody was planning, with reference to a certain man whose name was constantly mentioned yesterday, to call as a protected OTP witness. At the point in time when he contacted my associates and brought them the video of his interview as a suspect, and I published this in a book of mine, he never told us this. He was scared, because he knows that whoever ends up in The Hague Tribunal never gets out. So he brought some document, tried to wriggle out of it, brought other people to confirm his witness, brought them here, and this witness said so yesterday. There are several instances of this kind, but the fact that some people declared to be a protected witness, and these people have never been notified that they would actually be protected OTP witnesses, that's a problem. There's a man whose name I mentioned more than once yesterday who the OTP declared to be a protected witness, and in the statement I received from the OTP, it says that he refuses to be a Prosecution witness, that he would prefer to be a Defence witness. And this is contained in the statement disclosed to me by the OTP. And in spite of this, they declare him to be a Prosecution witness. The Prosecution cannot have a monopoly on all the people they ever interviewed. They interviewed some people as suspects, other people simply took down information. But a person makes a statement, and as soon as he does, he automatically becomes a Prosecution witness. How can this be? That can't be so. The person, himself, has to decide whose witness he wants to be, if he wants to be a witness, a Prosecution witness or a Defence witness. As soon as it was said that there would be no new indictments raised, these people took courage. They were no longer afraid, and then immediately they said they wanted to be Defence witnesses, not Prosecution witnesses, because they're no longer afraid of being indicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I think you're perhaps making a mistake. You are right, the OTP can no longer bring out new indictments. You are 100 per cent right on that. On the other hand, and the Rules of Procedure state this, the OTP, if they discover that a witness may have taken part in a crime against humanity, a war crime, or a crime relating to the Statute, can and should, indeed is duty-bound to send the procedure before the local prosecutor, and he or she can start up proceedings once again, inasmuch as a crime against humanity does not benefit from a Statue of Limitations. So when you assert, "Well, they have no fear of anything," I'm not as fully convinced as you are, and the best evidence of this, and you know this full well, there are indeed trials that are going on in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Croatia and in Serbia, against people who have committed this type of infringement. Some are ongoing. There will perhaps be others later. So to say that they have nothing to fear any longer, well, I am not as sure as you seem to be. Secondly, there's another point, and my fellow Judge pointed this out. Let's come back to this. You said on several occasions that sometimes there are actors who come along before this Court. You must have seen that I, and I think I'm the only one to do this in this Court, systematically I always ask the interested party, first of all, what his or her name is, surname, first name, function, title. I ask him or her whether he or she has been heard by other courts, and very soon to avoid the problem that we came up against yesterday, I will be asking them whether they have been judged and sentenced by other courts. Why do I do all this? Well, I do this, indeed, to avoid having before me a witness who does not have the identity that he or she is assumed to have. That's why I ask this type of question, and I think I'm one of the few ones who do this in this Court. And the history of judicial proceedings in some countries have, indeed, shown that some people have been sentenced under false identities or witness under false identities, and that's why I ask all these questions first. But on the other hand, if you have information about a witness, please do share -- or doubts, rather, about a witness, please do share these with us, and I will make sure that the witness shows us his or her passport. If you have any doubt whatsoever, please share these doubts with us so that we don't have to imagine that we are dealing with actors. Theoretically, it is possible, but if you exercise your control and if the panel also does its work, this will not arise. Mr. Seselj, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you have broached two problems here. The first is this: It is true that the people that were interviewed in the capacity of suspects and who really did commit certain crimes cannot be certain that once the mandate for the raising of new indictments is closed for the Prosecution, that they won't be indicted anymore, because pursuant to International Criminal Law for War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity, each Court is competent in the world and every country can initiate these proceedings if they seize a suspect or an accused. But if we're talking about people who have never perpetrated a crime, like Ljubisa Petkovic, for example, I can say, for example, Ljubisa Petkovic is this kind of man or that kind of man, but I can put my hand in the fire and say that he has never committed a crime of any sort, whereas the Prosecution puts the fear of God into him and he lives in fear until the Statue of Limitations expires for the raising of indictments. So that's the status of these people, and the vast sentences looming ahead of them, and then something clicks in their heads. Mr. President, I'm convinced that all of the charges in my indictment and everything stated in my indictment, and what the Prosecution has in its possession with respect to this indictment, no court in France, Italy, or Denmark would not hold me accountable and take me to task, initiate proceedings against me. It would be ludicrous for people like that to be brought before the tribunals, but you can do all this at the Hague Tribunal, and that is normal. Secondly, you say here that if I express doubts. Now, I'm surprised why you did not express doubts about the identity of those two Muslims who were victims and witnesses last week. If you look at the first statements they gave to the Muslim authorities, for example, neither of these witnesses remembered having given those statements. They had absolutely no idea about them. So doesn't that raise your doubts into their very identity? Whereas they remember all the details in their story related to the war, but when they came to the statements, where they were shown their statements, they had absolutely no idea about it. Now, they were asked to provide their passports. I think you've heard of the Zemun clan in Belgrade, the mafia clan that was held responsible for the killing of Djindjic. Djindjic was too a member of the mafia, but that's not important now. Some of them had Croatian passports, for example, not forged passports. They had officially-issued Croatian passports in false names, and that was established during the legal proceedings in Belgrade. Those passports were shown, they came to light. And now you think that something is proved on the basis of the passports. Well, the authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina or anywhere else can issue passports with any name you like. That's no proof or evidence at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let's end this. So you say -- you tell us today that there were two witnesses that came about whom you had doubts as to their identity. We take note of what you have said, and the panel will assess all this. At this stage, of course, we cannot draw any definite conclusions at all. Today, we are going to be looking at a series of videotapes. The OTP gave you the timetable for the videos that are distributed, like last time, on the basis of subject matter. Mr. Seselj, we would be very grateful if you would keep your comments to the minimum and either say, "I don't dispute this," or else you say, "I dispute this for such-and-such a reason," and to summarise those as far as possible. So don't start some major pleadings about a given videotape. You will have further opportunity to come back to them. So try and be efficient. Last time, things went quite smoothly, and today the same should be the case. Mr. Mundis, perhaps we can begin. Please proceed as you did last time. Tell us where the video comes from, its subject matter, and then we look at it. 19

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Dr. Seselj and everyone in and around the courtroom. The first collection of videotapes has been put under the theme of "Greater Serbia." This is 65 ter number 6002A, clip A. I note the time is indicated on the list that was distributed. That's actually the length of the entire tape. What we'll be showing is a clip that runs one minute and 10 seconds' long. This tape was received on or about 18 August 1999. It is from an unknown source. It is amateur footage of a speech made by Dr. Seselj in Dusseldorf, Germany. This is 65 ter 6002A, clip A, and the date of the video is approximately 8 August 1989.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "VS: I considered that the boundaries of the Serbian state could -- within Yugoslavia, or outside of Yugoslavia, if the Croats and Slovenians decide that the Yugoslav should not cease to exist can only be the borders which are internationally recognised, and the only internationally-recognised borders of Serbian statehood are the ones set out by the London agreement of 1915 in which the Western Allies guaranteed to the Serbian people a territorial expansion, a unification of all Serbian lands and all Serbian population, taking into account the enormous Serbian contribution to the overall allied effort in World War I. And this means ... And this means that the borders of the Serbian federal unit or the Serbian state must encompass not only the territories of the present so-called Narrower Serbia, but also Vojvodina, Kosovo, Metohija, Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Lika, Banija, Kordun, Eastern Slavonia and Baranja."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no comments to make, but this is footage from 1989, which is not a relevant year as far as the indictment is concerned. And the footage is fairly bad, it's a bad copy, but I'm grateful to the Prosecution for having found it, because I don't have that footage in my possession, I don't have it. So I would like to be disclosed that footage in its entirety, if at all possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number for this, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P325, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will certainly ensure that the accused gets a copy of that tape in its entirety. The next videotape to be shown bears 65 ter number 60004A. This is clip A. This tape runs approximately two and a half minutes' long. It was taken on or about 4 September 1989. It is a speech given by the accused in Hamilton, Canada, at the Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Nicholas. It is also amateur footage. It was received from the Open Society Archives, Central European University in Budapest, seized or received on 14 February 2003. Again, this is 65 ter number 6004A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "You mentioned the London agreement a moment ago. I have already somewhat forgotten history, it has been a long time since I studied it, but as you said, the border would be 0 Serbia. If Serbia would be a state, it would include Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun, Banija, Eastern Slavonia and Baranja. My question, considering present situation in Europe, how politically realistic would this be? Number 1, if Serbia were to be a separate state, and even if it were to be a part of the Yugoslav Federation, how realistic would it be for the Serbs to be able to achieve this? My second question is this: Since I went to school in Yugoslavia, I was in Split, later I went to Belgrade, one of the greatest dangers for the Serbian people in Croatia is quiet assimilation, because we're simply in a minority over there, our script has been neglected, and our religion was suppressed. The situation is probably different now, and I believe this is one of the biggest problems and an issue which should be given due attention, because until we become part of a larger Serbian community, we are more or less left in the lurch. Thank you. "Very well. As far as your second question is concerned, you gave the answer yourself right away, and basically I agree with you. And as far as the first question is concerned, how realistic it is to realise the Serbian borders as guaranteed by the London Agreement, I think that the present international political situation in Europe is perfectly suited for us, because we are not threatened by the possibility of a foreign military intervention either from the East or West. The Soviet Union and her allies are preoccupied with their internal problems, and I suppose they would never dream of intervening militarily here in Yugoslavia, regardless of what happens here. The Soviet Union was forced to withdraw from Afghanistan. "I also think that this is not the moment when there is a threat of armed intervention from the Western powers, so that fortunately all of us living in Yugoslavia are left to our own devices. So we will see what our heroes' fortune brings, and God hold us in this test."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two comments to make. The first is this: You see what technology can do? This quite obviously is not my voice. It's like one of the voices of your protected witnesses here, which is distorted to avoid being recognised. Now, how this came about in this particular footage, I don't know, but can you imagine if you gave this tape to a witness to listen to and ask him whether he recognises it as being me speaking or not? Now, the Prosecution intends to play some intercepted telephone conversations to see if they can be identified, and I say that is impossible. Telephone conversations can only be identified by professionals or with the people actually speaking. Secondly, this could not have been in Hamilton, Canada. That's absolutely impossible, because in September 1989 I was not in Canada. I was in Canada that same year, but in the month of May, whereas in September 1989 I was somewhere in Western Europe. Where, I can't say exactly, because I made a tour of Great Britain, France, Germany, Switzerland -- well, those four countries. Now, where this was, I really can't remember now. Quite obviously, it's me on the tape. I can see the date. I don't doubt the date, either. But it cannot be Canada. So I don't know how you can identify this without the Prosecution finding the exact facts as to where this was and when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, someone is asking you two questions. The first is directly related to the London Agreement, and the second is a question about Serbs in Croatia whose religion is suppressed, allegedly, and the alphabet also neglected. Someone answers, and I thought it was you. And you're saying that it wasn't you, that it's not your voice. Someone answers, saying -- well, the second question, the answer is obvious, and the person who's answering immediately goes on to the first question, saying, there's no risk, either from the East or the West. The Russians cannot intervene, and their allies can't either, for such-and-such a reason, and the Western forces can't either. So there's nothing very special in that answer. But where I'm amazed is where you say, "It's not my voice," you're disputing that the answer given was your voice. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in court you listen to my voice, you can hear my voice in court, in the courtroom, and just listen to the voice on the tape. I didn't say it wasn't my voice. I said that through certain technological procedures, my voice was modified or distorted. It is me on the tape, and the contents of the speech are mine, but why has my voice been distorted? I rather like the voice I heard. It's even deeper than my deep and strong voice, which I'm very proud of, and this is an even deeper voice. Can you imagine if I spoke like that every day in court here, with that deep, deep voice? So I'm asking the question of why my voice has been distorted there. Why has it been modified? I'm not challenging the fact that it is, in fact, my voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, according to Mr. Seselj, his voice has been distorted, and he is formally disputing that this could have happened on the 4th of September in Canada, Hamilton, because he wasn't there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, all I can indicate is the information that is contained on what is called our MIF or ERN registration system as to where we got the tape and the description that the investigator entered into the system upon obtaining the tape. So I certainly can't stand here and give you evidence as to whether or not this was actually in Canada. All I can do is convey information that is contained within the Prosecution's Evidence Unit concerning this material. With respect to the concern over the possibility of the tape or the voice being distorted, again, I don't know. I was, to be honest, listening to the English channel and not the original. Perhaps we can play it again. I will say, as I said last week or the week before, the quality of many videotapes deteriorates over time. Perhaps the tape, when it was digitised, was run at a slightly slower speed than normal, which of course causes human voices to sound deeper than they actually are, or it could be a question of the tape, actually at the time it was digitised, the quality of the tape had degraded such that the voice sounds to be or seems to be distorted. I don't know the answer to that question. I assure you that no one within the Office of the Prosecutor has distorted tapes in order to alter the sounds of the accused's voice. I can certainly give you that assurance. So the tape is what it is. It speaks for itself. I'm happy to play that clip again if the Chamber would like to hear it again to listen to the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it's necessary. Shall we give it an MFI number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it stands, we won't accept it because of the objections, but we will be giving it an MFI number. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P326 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll actually at this point seek some guidance from the Trial Chamber. The next two clips on the list are obtained from the same original tape or the same source, they are simply different clips. We can either play them and again most likely have the same objections, or we can simply skip them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The best is, indeed, to listen to them, and we'll give them MFI numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip is 65 ter number 6004B. Again, I won't repeat where we got it from. It's part of -- it's simply another clip from the same longer-running Q-and-A session. So this is 65 ter number 6004B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "As far as the borders of the Serbian Federal Unit are concerned they are determined as borders of the Serbian State by the London pact. Borders guaranteed by the Western Allies to Serbia for its enormous contribution to the victory over the axis forces, that is, the forces of the central pact. And these borders of the Serbian state, according to the London Agreement, encompass not only the present-day -- not only present-day Serbia proper, as a somewhat extended Belgrade province, but also Vojvodina, Kosovo, Metohija, Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia, Herzegovina, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Lika, Banija, Kordun, Eastern Slavonia and Baranja."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the possibility exists that I might actually have spoken that way. Perhaps my voice was like that at one time, and perhaps in the intervening six years while I've been in detention in The Hague, they gave me some wrong medicaments or hormones which led to a voice change. So that might be grounds for a new investigation. Now, this reminds me of the voice of the late Russian General Alexander Lebed who was a presidential candidate at the elections in Russia in 1996, and after that he was killed, I think, in a traffic accident. Well, I've just heard General Lebed with a deep voice like that, or perhaps I'd operated -- had an operation on my throat. Usually, when you have cancer surgery and take your vocal chords -- your vocal chords are taken out, you have a special apparatus to replace them, and that's how your voice sounds. I don't know what else it could be, what other reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall now give an MFI number to this document. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P327 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just an observation so that this appears on the transcript. The "P325," which is the first video we saw, is dated the 8th of August, 1989, and relates to the borders arising from the London Agreement. That video, which apparently was shot on the 4th of September, 1989, because we see the date on the tape, in fact restates what was said in the London Agreement and adds other elements. That's all we can say about this. We don't know where it took place. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip, Your Honours, is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may raise another objection. This previous clip again I'm not sure is dated properly, because I remember this tour of mine. It began in the beginning of August 1989 in England. However, I'm not sure that by the 8th of August, I had already arrived in Dusseld orf. It should have been a bit later, because I stayed in England for a few days, and then from England I went to Munich, and then I toured all of Germany and visited Dusseldorf towards the end of the tour, and then I went back to England via France. The tour began and ended in England. So the date is suspect, the 8th of August. It may have been in August, but a little later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That has been taken on record. The next clip, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honours, the next clip is 65 ter number 6004C. This again, as with the two preceding clips, comes from the same tape. This is 65 ter 6004C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, my case manager informs me that we need to restart that so that the subtitles work properly at the bottom of the tape. So if we could please play that one again from the beginning. Mr. President, we seem to be having some problems getting these subtitles to work properly. I know it's a bit early. Perhaps we should take our first break at this point in time in order to see if we can get some technical assistance to make the presentation go a little more smoothly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a break, and we'll have the gods of technology solve everything at the moment during the break, and we'll meet again in 20 minutes, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing may resume. I believe the technical problem has been overcome. I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe the gods of technology have smiled upon us today. The next clip is 65 ter number 6004C.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I gave an extensive lecture on this topic, you know, because the majority of people here today have already heard this previous lecture. I was mainly not adding things, but I can give you a short answer. I believe what is necessary is a new colonization of Kosovo and Metohija which would involve the transfer of the Serbian and Yugoslav capital to Kosovo Metohija, most likely Pristina, which would also cause hundreds of thousands of state employees, civil servants, and members of their families to move, all state institutions and establishments, then the transfer of all the military and police academies and military institutions, which would cause the move of several thousands of officers, non-commissioned officers and policemen, and their families to Kosovo and Metohija. "I also supported the expulsion from Yugoslavia of all 360.000 Albanians immigrants who came to Kosovo and Metohija after April 6, 1941, also for the nationalisation of an agricultural belt running along the Albanian border, let's say some 50, maybe even 100 kilometres long, considering that state interests of Serbia and Yugoslavia require this because the Albanian national minority has, in most cases, proved itself unable to come to terms with the Serbian and Yugoslav sovereignty on this vital territory of ours. I don't think that all Albanians are like that, but the majority of them have separatist tendencies, but their numbers are negligible. That is in a couple of -- they can go to Croatia and Slovenia, since there they like them best, they can support them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there's nothing here to indicate where or when this speech was held, and the OTP is unable to identify this. However, looking at this speech, and I can see how clever it was, I regret that I didn't come to power in time, have political power, and implement this plan. Then we would have avoided all wars. I see that my main problem is that I didn't come to power in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, are you in favour or against the admission of this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not opposed to admitting into evidence any clip where I can be seen and where I am speaking. But I am raising these objections for the benefit of the Chamber. The voice has been modified in an inadmissible manner, and the OTP is unable to say when or where this clip was taken. You can see that the clips are not all from the same place. They're all marked "Hamilton," but evidently it isn't Hamilton. Either it is Hamilton but not this state or it's some other place. I visited many places in Canada, Hamilton, Toronto, Montreal, and many small towns in the interior where there are Serbian communities, but the OTP should identify the places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll give an MFI number, then. If later on the OTP could find a date for this recording, as well as a place, we would lift the MFI. But may we have an MFI number for the moment, Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P328 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 327 or 328, because the last one was 327. It must be 328, P328. Would you please say it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. Exhibit P328 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6007. This is, we believe, undated, but it is sometime in 1991. This is a documentary -- or from a documentary called "Speerspitze, Serbians, produced by Austrian Television, received from the open society archives on 4 June 2003. This clip runs a little bit longer than two minutes. Unlike the previous tape, this tape does not show Dr. Seselj speaking, but does show an individual whom an earlier witness has identified as one of Dr. Seselj's men. This is 65 ter number 6007.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Commander Ljuban used to be a carrier and barkeeper. He's prepared for a long war. "I expect the whole affair will be over in two years. "Why so long? "Nobody can create a neutral zone in an area here which has to be cleansed, purged, and then separated in a short time."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that this is German and she's unable to check whether the translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that the speaker is speaking in German, and we therefore cannot translate from German, although we have, of course, the text in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tell the French booth that we have two French booths working simultaneously and translating simultaneously. One of the French booths will translate, and that will be enough. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is absolutely inadmissible for several reasons. First of all, we heard nothing of what these people were saying. We heard only the interpreters interpreting a subtitled text. Secondly, what witness in the courtroom here identified this Ljuban Macakanja, as it says here. This is the first time I've heard this name, and I have no idea who this man is. Secondly, Sava Grujic is mentioned here as a Serb volunteer and lawyer. I knew Sava Grujic, from Novi Sad. He was never a member of the Serbian Radical Party, but he was the president of some sort of patriotic organisation of which I don't recall the name right now. The name is well known, but it has nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party. Nothing is known about this clip, where, when, how, or why it was taped. None of these people has been identified as being a member of the Serbian Radical Party, so this clip is absolutely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will not accept this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip indicated on the list, Your Honours, indicates it was previously admitted as P2, bearing 65 ter number 6015. The indication that it was P2 is erroneous. What was previously shown and admitted was clip E from the same tape. What we're now proposing to play is clip A from this tape. So the marking on the list indicating this has previously been admitted is not correct. We will now show 65 ter number 6015A, which is clip A from the same videotape. This clip runs approximately 79 seconds. The originator was the AID, Sarajevo. The submission date or the date of receipt in OTP was 27 August 1998. This is 65 ter number 6015A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "According to you, there were two or three key determinants of the party that you're at the head of. Firstly, the Serbian Radical Party and its collective members, the Serbian Chetnik Movement, the Serbian Cultural Club, the Serbian Women's Volunteer Association, the Serbian Renaissance and the Sokol Society and the Peasants Association are in favour of -- and we consider that even when you include Vojvodina and Kosovo and Metohija, the state should include Serbian-Macedonia, Serbian-Montenegro, Serbian-Bosnia, Serbian-Herzegovina, Serbian-Dubrovnik, Serbian-Dalmatia, Serbian-Lika, Serbian-Banija, Serbian-Kordun, Serbian-Slavonia and Serbian-Banija, and then in the political sphere we're fighting for a democratic and free society with a multi-party system, a modern legal system, and citizens' freedom and rights. We have an economic programme based on re-privatisation, paying off foreign debts, and giving full ownership of a suitable number of our factories to foreign creditors. Then we have a very complete social program, a national program, and particularly a program for resolving or rather crushing Albanian separatist insurrection in Kosovo and Metohija and other things."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, but I can give you a piece of information, if you're interested. Here, along with the Serbian Chetnik Movement, I'm also referring to another section of the Serbian Radical Party, but this is May 1991, when the party had just been registered, and we were too ambitious in our approach to setting up these sections within the party. We then gave it all up, except for the Serbian Chetnik Movement, which lasted until 1994. All the other sections never actually began to function within the party. This is simply to avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P329, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we go forward, because I don't want to forget, I want to express our extreme gratitude to the interpreters who have to follow these videotapes at a relatively fast pace, and we do appreciate their efforts. The next clip or tape is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] AID, Sarajevo, that's the Secret Services of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That was the former name, yes, the Agency for Information and Documentation. That was the former name of the intelligence services. It no longer goes by that name, but at the time we received the material, yes, "AID" was the Bosnian intelligence service. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6019 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. As this service has been mentioned, its name was "IAD." Everyone who's heard of it knows it under that name. I mentioned it when the two Muslim witnesses were heard here. This is a service that prepares witnesses and tutors them for their testimony before this Tribunal. It coaches them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So it's "IAD" and not "AID"?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's called "Aid." You know, in the Serbian language, you can create a word out of an abbreviation. This is A-I-D in English, in the English alphabet, but in the Serbian language, when you have a three-letter abbreviation, you can pronounce it as if it were a word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Certainly, in English, it is in fact known as A-I-D. Of course, the Prosecution would not agree with the accused when he indicates that they prepare or coach witnesses for their testimony. I will put that on the record. The next clip is 65 ter number 6019A. The date of this tape is 1 June 1991. This is clip A from this tape. It runs approximately two minutes and six seconds. It's from TV Novi Sad, from a television programme called "NS Plus." This is the second of three videotapes connected to a collection of information and data from the Croatian Ministry of the Interior from a video entitled "Vojislav Seselj, HRT Archive Material." The collection of information and data was sent to the Tribunal or to the OTP on 20 March 1996 by the War Crimes Commission, Zagreb, pursuant to a request of the Office of the Prosecutor dated 19 February 1996. This is 65 ter number 6019A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Vez na Radovanvic, what sort of future do you see for Yugoslavia and what is your position with regard to the nations that constitute Serbia? "Well, I don't think Yugoslavia has any future. I think there are two possibilities with or in regard to this question. In any event, Yugoslavia will cease to exist, I am profoundly convinced of this. The first possibility is that Yugoslavia will split up into three states: A greater Serbia, a small Slovenia and an even smaller Croatia. If the Croats don't like this idea, the second possibility is for us Serbs to come to an agreement with Italians and establish a Serbian-Italian border on the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-and-Virovitica line and it is only fair to return to the Italians what is theirs. We could also talk to the Hungarians and the Austrians. Austria is interested in gaining access to the sea through Austria and Germany, and it would probably be fair to grant this to Austria. But we shall certainly talk to the Hungarians, because they have certain historical rights. There was a time when the Croats themselves handed over their state to the Hungarians, who built a big port on the Adriatic coast in the last century called Rijeka, so perhaps it would be fair to give Rijeka back to the Hungarians. It all depends on how these neighbouring states of ours behave. So far, they haven't behaved well at all. You see the Austrians support our enemies, the Hungarians help Croatia to arm itself. Their governments are short-sighted, not to use a worse expression. Whereas if they want to obtain certain objective, the Serbs are their natural allies. They, let's say the Hungarians, will never be able to get even a part of Vojvodina. That's something they've got to understand. The only territory they could get is there in the west, Rijeka, which is beyond the Croatian Zagorije region, could provide them with access to the Adriatic Sea. Only the Serbs could be allies in this case, which is why they should think about their policies. If the Hungarians and the Austrians don't change their attitude, we'll come to an agreement with Italy."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the OTP should have disclosed this material to me under Rule 68(1) as exculpatory material, because it shows what a just person I was in analysing international relations. I wanted to resolve all these ancient historical injustices towards Italy, Austria, and Hungary. So this, in fact, is exculpatory material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become Exhibit P330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as to the source from which this material came, I have something to say. A few years ago, I applied to the then Trial Chamber, and I think, Mr. President, you were then a member of that Chamber, to issue a subpoena obliging the government in Zagreb and the Muslim government in Sarajevo, as well as the governments of some Western countries, to disclose to me, for the needs of my defence, all the materials their intelligence services have where my name or the name of the Serbian Radical Party is mentioned. And the Trial Chamber rejected this motion. I cannot ask anything from Croatia directly because Croatia is a hostile state. I can neither ask it for anything, nor contact it, nor can any of my legal associates contact it or travel there. Secondly, the USA, France, and Great Britain are a special problem, because they have many documents in their archives. I have sent official requests. The Americans sent me a reply. They've already calculated how much it would cost and what the methodology would be to request this. I am unable to pay for this. I delivered to a Trial Chamber the response of the US government. The other governments, the governments of France and Great Britain, turned a deaf ear to my application, which was sent to them through their embassies in Belgrade. I think they have an abundance of documentation and that much of it would be exculpatory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding this, you are right, I was in Chamber number 2. I don't have a specific knowledge of this submission, because you made thousands of them. You know, you'd have to have the memory of an elephant to remember everything. But today there is a new Trial Chamber, and my position is extremely clear. You're entitled to ask a government to disclose to you documents that they have. Then you request, and the government will answer. It seems that the Americans have answered you, but they're asking you to pay, which you want. If you are running into difficulties, then you can make a submission to the Chamber and file a motion, and the Chamber will have -- is able -- is entitled to subpoena the government, and the government will see whether it wants to make sure that some documents remain confidential, as under Article 70, and there's a procedure for that. So if you did not get an answer, you could always file a motion to the Trial Chamber, tell us what is happening, give us a copy of all the mail that might have been exchanged, and then you make a new request in good order. Then the Trial Chamber will seize the state involved, and this state, because of cooperation requirements, must provide the documents. There's no reason why a state could give the OTP documents and not provide the accused with documents, since the document [as interpreted] should have the same access to documents as the OTP, of course subject to the reservation that states might want to restrict some documents because of confidentiality. There are documents that could be declassified, on the other hand. There are countries where commissions have been set up. For example, in my country there are commissions that are there to rule as to the declassification of documents. So there are a lot of opportunities and possibilities that are open to you. As far as I'm concerned, I will look into this request -- into this motion that was denied in order to know why it was denied at the time. Maybe the reasons why it was denied at the time no longer apply. But remember, you have a possibility, through the Rules, to do something, and the Trial Chamber will do its utmost, of course, to help you have access to documents which you may require for your defence. Let's now move to the next video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next videotape bears 65 ter number 6022A, 6022A. This clip is dated 21 June 1991. It runs approximately two minutes. It is material that was originally from Radio-Television Serbia. The Prosecution received it on 1 May 1995. This is 65 ter number 6022A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The leader of the Serbian Radical Party, people's deputy Dr. Vojislav Seselj, says he supported the sending of peace forces to Yugoslavia, but to the western borders of Serbia with Croatia. "What else was discussed with representatives of the fourth estate? "The president of the Serbian Radical Party, Dr. Vojislav Seselj, welcomed the proclamation renewal of the Republic of Dubrovnik, the establishment of its government, and its decision to remain within Yugoslavia. At a press conference in Pristina, Seselj stated that the Serbian Radical Party welcomed the decision of the presidency of Yugoslavia to invite the blue helmets, but demanded that they be deployed on the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-and-Virovitica line and by no means on the borders of the Avnoj, Tito's Yugoslavia. On this occasion as well Seselj called on all Serb patriots to go to the front, especially to Western Slavonia. However, he believes that volunteers from Kosovo and Metohija should not be sent there. Serbs from Kosovo and Metohija must remain here in strength and be well-organised, armed, and trained to nip in the bud any possible uprising of Albanian separatists. The Serbian Radical Party also warns all members of the Siptar national minority and the members of the Croatian minority on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija that there can be no life in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija for those families whose members are serving in the Ustasha Armed Forces, the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia, or the National Guard Corps of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm grateful to the Prosecution for having come by this footage. I didn't have it in my own archives, and I would like to have it in its entirety, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Prosecutor, please disclose the entire footage to Mr. Seselj. And could the Registrar please give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P331.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip bears 65 ter number 6025C, 6025C. This is from July 1991, from TV "Politika." This was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor on 19 September 2003 by a protected witness in this case. This is 65 ter number 6025C.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "These are now unified volunteer detachments that go under the patronage of the Association of Serbs from Croatia and they now have no party-related markings. These volunteer detachments have their own uniforms and symbols, of course no five-pointed star at all, the symbols of the Serbian four S with a cross on the cap, on the sleeve, and here on the tunic. "And these units shall operate -- dress the same way. The members of the Serbian Radical Party, the Chetnik Movement, Serb National Renewal, Serbian Democratic Party and National Party and other volunteers from other parties will be among them, we draw no distinction between them, even the ones who are not party organised. So all those who are ready to fight for these fundamental patriotic ideals of ours."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Mr. Seselj, it's unfortunate that the camera that was zooming in on the insignia on the shirt worn by Mr. Seselj all of a sudden stopped. It would have been interesting to actually see that insignia, because according to what Mr. Seselj is saying, the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party have that insignia. That's what I understood. So, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you didn't understand this in the best possible way. I have the traditional Serbian coat of arms on my chest. In this case, it was gold, a golden one. So not the kinds that were sold on the streets as a souvenir, but a specially-manufactured one for Chetnik Vojvoda. Now, I indicate where the new symbol is worn, the symbol that the Association of Serbs from Croatia decided to wear, the cross with the C-scroll or S-scroll ornamentation, which is also the traditional Serbian symbol. And when we're talking about a double-headed eagle, then he has this same symbol on his breasts, and I am pointing to where it is worn on the uniform, not the coat of arms that I had like the one that was agreed upon. Now, I have an objection here. I would like to have this admitted into evidence, but I must give you my comments and objections. This is a time which is not relevant for the indictment, because the indictment goes after the 1st of August, 1991. That's what it's based on. And according to their concept of the alleged joint criminal enterprise, from the point in time that the Serbian Radical Party cooperates with the JNA. Now, this is a time when the JNA was not included in the conflict at all, so we have several phases, and I think this is important for you to understand. We have the first stage, where the Serbian Radical Party sends certain groups of volunteers to defend Serb villages. That is from April 1991 onwards. Now, in July, it becomes -- the Association of Serbs from Croatia becomes involved with its headquarters in Cviceva [phoen] Street Belgrade, and it tries to conjoin the efforts of all the political parties in that direction, and wants these volunteers not to have any party affiliation symbols, but to be a uniform and that the state of the volunteers be uniformed. And that was in July, and you had the document dating to the end of August or beginning of September, where Ljubisa Petkovic ask that all volunteers be returned to Belgrade so as to have re-organisation take place, and an agreement was reached with the JNA in the background that in future all volunteers should be sent through the JNA. And I think that was important for me to clarify, although it's not the right comment to make, looking at the footage itself. But I do agree that the footage can be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are in agreement under the proviso of the remarks you just made. Let's give this document a number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P332.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 6025D. The date of this clip is 25 July 1991. This is clip E from this tape. Again, this tape came to us from a protected witness. The Prosecution received the tape on 19 September 2003.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Everything that happened in that republic, Seselj says, we blame Ante Markovic, because what happened in Slovenia was another deception against the Serbian people with the aim to besmirch the Serbian weapons to accuse the Serbian people. He condemns the move to send 19-year-olds into military operations as being conducted in Slovenia. That is why the Serbian Radical Party rues over the innocent blood that is being shed. The Vojislav Seselj is asking himself why the army intervened Slovenia and not in Croatia, which would be logical as far as he's concerned, as in Croatia and Ustasha false government was constituted where genocide has been started. And Ante Markovic, he says, wanted to spare his republic. "Seselj blames the Serbian leadership, too, because they accepted the conditions and ultimatums. The Serbian Radical Party will never accept the Stipe Mesic as president of the Yugoslav Presidency, and believes neither will the Serbian people. "Answering the many questions by journalists, Vojislav Seselj said, among other things, that the Serbian Radical Party has no volunteer units in Serbia proper but that they are going to continue to support the Serbs in Krajina, Baranja, Slavonia, and Srem, not only financially. 'We will send volunteers,' says Seselj, to those places where they are most needed. "Scheduled for the July the 17th is a large commemoration on the occasion on the occasion of the 50th anniversary of the death of General Draza Mihajlovic in front of the Prince Mihailo monument in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We hear the journalist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no interpretation in English, so we'll start all over again. So I'll start over again, since there was no English interpretation. It is working now. Good. So the Chamber observes that what is going on is a press conference with a lot of journalists there drinking fruit juice and Coke, but we don't actually hear Mr. Seselj speaking. The journalist is the one who seems to be summarising what Mr. Seselj said during the same press conference. That's what we can see. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two objections. First, it seems that the Prosecution cuts off this footage in a crucial place, because I would have liked to see what the continuation of the tape was, but they withheld that pleasure for me. And it's a little -- it lacks seriousness to say that this is the 27th of July, 1991. This must have been far earlier than that, because you can see here that the journalist is interpreting my words, that we were going to organise a large commemorative meeting in Belgrade to mark the anniversary of the execution of General Draza Mihajlovic, which was the 17th of June, so this must have been a few days before the 17th of July. It could not have been on the 25th of July. I could not be saying this then; that is to say, eight days after the commemorative meeting was held, to announce that a commemorative meeting would be held. And that's what I keep telling you here. The Prosecutor receives a tape, receives a date, and takes it to be the right thing, whereas they would have to check it out to see whether it was the truth, whether it was broadcast on Television Serbia, to ask explanations, to determine the exact date, so that we don't have this contradiction appearing in the tape itself and the attending text. So it's not the 25th of July, but several days before the 17th of July, in fact. And I agree that it be admitted, regardless of the fact that the journalist -- there's a voiceover by the journalist who is interpreting it. I think it's fairly reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Inasmuch as the journalist's interpretation seems to you to be reliable, under the proviso that the date is not right, you do not object, so we can go on and give it a number. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 6025E. Again, there's an error on the list. This should be "6025E." This is clip D from the same tape obtained from the same witness on 19 September 2003. This clip, which runs a little bit less than two minutes, was originally broadcast on Radio-Television Serbia, RTS. Again, 65 ter number 6025E.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Unless we're serious enough at the level of historical requirements, we will waste a historic chance of the Serbian people. Whether we are aware of the situation into which this historic whirlwind has thrown us or not, that is a secondary issue. We are here. We have to take a serious position in the matter. This time, if we gamble away our chance, we will definitely lose. The boundaries that the West will have established in five, ten days, or a month, they will remain the final boundaries within which the Serbian people will live. That is why we must not gamble with it. Karlobag-Ogulin- Karlovac-and-Virovitica, that line must be our choice and that is the border to which the army must withdraw all its troops. If they are not in a position to withdraw them from Zagreb without combat, they should engaging in combat and shelling Zagreb. The army has enough capacities it has not used at all. If the troops are in danger, it has the right to use napalm bombs and everything else from its storage, and we must not be playing games in that regard. It is more important to save a military unit than to worry about some accidental victims will fall there. Well, whose fault is it? They wanted the war, they have it. The army must withdraw from Slovenia and from Croatia, from Rijeka. The Rijeka Corps must pull out from Zagreb as well. Where -- everywhere where Croats live, the army has business in territories that are not ours. Once the army has withdrawn to the line which we consider our western border, it will become an invincible army."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have three objections or, rather, comments. First of all, why has the footage been made smaller and a landscape shown? I think it's the landscape of Belgrade. That's unnecessary. I think the full footage from the Assembly should be shown, because the Assembly holds all its sessions with their transcripts. So it shouldn't have been third-hand and handed down that way. Secondly, you can see that I behave here just like American General Wesley Clark, except he was an aggressor on foreign territory and I'm defending my own territory, my own country. And as to collateral damage, none of us took that into account when we invoked the assistance of the Air Force, to the great sorrow of The Hague Tribunal and everybody else, I had no power over the Air Force otherwise, this war would have ended quite differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So do you accept that it be tendered?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... everything that testifies to my prominent historical role in the Balkan crisis, I am in favour of being admitted into evidence and save for future generations in every way possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Chamber, too, not just for the future generations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know that I'm more interested in history than a court judgement or court proceedings or anything like that. I have ceased to live a normal life. I'm living a great historical life, and all that's left to me now is history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, yes, Mr. Seselj, but sometimes history is also made up out of judgements. That is why we need to have evidence. Well, so we shall have this video entered into the file, and the Registrar will give it a number now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P334.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6041C. The date of this tape is 23 November 1991. It is clip C. It runs approximately two and a half minutes. It was originally broadcast on TV Benkovac it was received from the Croatian government in 2001, 65 ter number 6041C.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "A message to the Serbian people in Benkovacka Krajina. I'm very pleased that the Serbs here are holding together and are unified, that they are so decisive to endure in this justified battle against this uncontrollably wild beast embodied in Ustashas. I am happy that you represent dignity and honour of the Serbian people here, at the outermost boundaries of the defence of Serbdom. I'm happy that the Serbs here will not give up this fight, and I am happy because the Serbian Zadar will once again be in Serbian hands. Stay together and preserve unity. Do not allow anybody shake you, divide you, or tear you apart. We shall help as much as needed and as much as we can in cooperation with the army and our volunteers. Serbian Chetniks and your territorial defence members, the whole of the Serbian people will triumph because the Croats are no match for us. They only know how to commit crimes. They've never learnt to win in a chivalrous fashion on the battlefield. "What can you say about the political turmoil in Krajina, and do you have a message to the whole of the Serbian people in relation to that political turmoil? "This is not the time for political turmoil, conflicts and divisions. We must endure in harmony and unity, and when we win we will all get our place according to the results at the democratic elections. If you lose, you lose, and there's nothing to be done about it, but before the victory is achieved, nobody has the right to put their personal interests before the interests of the Serbian people. I am convinced that your most important political leaders, Dr. Milan Babic and Milan Martic, will find a way to communicate, and that together they will bring this struggle to an end, the struggle the two of them started. I am also convinced that their accord and unity will serve as an example to all other Serbs. All in all, there is no room for Ustashas among us or with us. There is no room for Ustashas in neither in Serbia Zadar or in Serbian Sibenik. Those are Serbian territories, Serbian people live there, and I hope I will spend my summer vacation at the Serbian seaside next year in Serbian Zadar."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've already seen excerpts from one unified tape, and you will remember my conflict with Captain Dragan at the frontline at Zadar, between Benkovac and Zadar, in fact. And now the question arises of why the Prosecution is dividing this up. Why didn't we have the entire tape shown, because all this was taken with one camera, Serbian Television Benkovac camera, my arrival in Benkovac, my journey to the frontline, the appearance of Captain Dragan, my conflict with him, meetings with the combatants afterwards, and the statement for Television Benkovac. So why has this been divided up into small sections? It would have been much better if we could have seen the tape in its entirety and then have it admitted into evidence in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I derive from that that you're not against this being tendered into evidence, but you make us notice that it would have been better to have the recording in its entirety, in particular the part where you are seen to challenge Captain Dragan. So we've put this into the transcript, and now let's allocate a number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit P335.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something else to add, Judges. This tape is very important to me, in its entirety it's important, because it shows where I was when Vukovar was liberated, it shows my whereabouts. I was 300 or 400 kilometres away. I went to Banja Luka by helicopter, then Western Slavonia. From Western Slavonia, I went by car to Knin, and then from Knin by helicopter to Mostar, and then from Mostar by helicopter to Podgorica, and then towards the end of November from Podgorica I returned to Belgrade by plane.
