So this tape, in its total, is important to me, and I would like you to give instructions to the Prosecution to provide the tape in its entirety, because then you can see the context. But when you put it out of context and just show excerpts of one or two minutes, you can't see the context in which the entire film was taped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, the entire recording, how long does it last?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One hour and nine minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can assure the Trial Chamber that this tape, in its entirety, if it hasn't already been disclosed to Dr. Seselj, will be disclosed to him, and he, of course, will be at liberty to play the one hour and ten-minute tape during the Defence case, if he so chooses. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6008A, again from 1991. This clip runs approximately one minute and seven seconds. It was originally broadcast on RTS, Radio-Television Serbia. Again, the tape was received from a witness on 20 December 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "All I --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In the fighting for Milovo Brdo near Vukovar against Croatian separatist rebels, Serbian volunteers suffered two men killed, 11 injured. Putting forward his party's stance on the arrival of the blue helmets, Petkovic said that those forces must be deployed west of the Karlobag-Ogulin-Karlovac-Virovitica border and that there must not be any soldiers in those units who are from countries which are hostile to us. The Serbian Radical Party has assessed that the Yugoslav People's Army has consolidated its forces, but at the same time it was requested that General Kadijevic and Admiral Brovet resign. In reference to the government in Serbia, it was said that it should be given support and assistance and that it may be changed only once the war is over and the western Serbian is established. At the end of the conference, journalists were appraised of the information accusing General Ante Markovic. Because of the fact, as they state, he worked against the country's interest, the Serbian Radical Party requests that the state security of Serbia to ban the federal prime minister from entering Serbia."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, an objection. We have a very interesting tape, but at the most interesting point the Prosecutor cuts it off. He keeps saying that the tape was received from witnesses. No, it was not. From suspects, it was obtained from suspects, and he should say that. They received the tape from a suspect, and that particular suspect will never be a Prosecution witness, he will be a Defence witness. Otherwise, I have no objection to having this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall give a number to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P336.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next tape bears 65 ter number 6047A, 6047A. The date of this tape is 30 January 1992. The clip runs two minutes' long from Radio-TV Belgrade. The material originally came from the SFRY Television. It was submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor on 1 April 1996. This is 65 ter number 6047A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "'The Serbian Radical Party will at no cost allow the independent state of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the present borders,' said Vojislav Seselj at a press conference. According to him, there are two options for this republic, to remain a federal unit within the rump of Yugoslavia or to be divided among the ethnicities living in it on the basis of the principle of majority domination in respective territories. The Serbian Radical Party will not accept the results of the referendum and the further insisting of Bosnia and Herzegovina leadership on that could lead, as Seselj claims, to bloodshed even greater than happened on battlefields of Croatia and Krajina. "Seselj called upon the Serbs of Bosnia-Herzegovina to boycott the referendum. He proposed the same to the Muslims in order to avoid, as he said, the participation in adventurism and megalomania of the BiH leadership. Seselj condemned the federal authorities following their actions related to the citizens' foreign currency, savings accounts, and passed on the requests of his party to the federal -- federation to guarantee the citizen's savings accounts with all its assets. "Seselj reproached the Serbian government for not allowing the opening of the free zone in Serbia and regarding the decision to freeze prices and salaries, saying it could be nothing good. Commenting on the arrival of the blue helmets, as Seselj said, 'We do not categorically oppose their deployment on Serbian territory. As a party, we generally accepted the Vance plan because we consider it a far lesser evil than intervention by the European community and that in any case Vance's plan assures that Serbian Krajina no longer be a part of the Croatian state, the independent state of Croatia, and that the independent state of Croatia would never again be able to control Serbian Krajina.' "With respect to the demonstrations by the volunteers in Belgrade, Seselj was categoric, 'If they take part in the demonstration the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Movement and Chetnik party will be excluded from the party or movement.'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a number of objections. First of all, I think that this should have been under 68(1) ter exculpatory material, that it should have been disclosed to me under that Rule. Secondly, you can see a meeting of volunteers which was scheduled is mentioned here that the witness spoke about, that testified about here yesterday, and you can see how the party distanced itself from this and said that anybody taking part would be excluded from the party. And there was a small rally of just 15 or 20 people once it was held, but I think that's important so that you can link it up to the testimony of yesterday's witness. Thirdly, the Prosecutor every time speaks about the source of the tape, whereas this time he doesn't provide the source, because he was ashamed to say that it was Natasha Kandic who provided this video footage. I now understand why the Prosecutor is ashamed. I would be ashamed, too, if I collaborated with Natasha Kandic in any shape or form. So I agree that this footage be admitted into evidence. I'd just like to draw your attention once again to this. You see how naive we Serbs are when we believed in the United Nations, whereas the United Nations tricked us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall now give a number, Madam Registrar, to this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become Exhibit P337, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minor observation, Mr. Seselj. You say that this document was provided by Natasha Kandic and that the OTP didn't want to mention that. Let me just point out that in the list, I saw another video that was handed over by Natasha Kandic, and that was pointed out there. So why would the Prosecutor give the origin of one video and not the other? I don't -- I wouldn't really understand what the rationale would be, but perhaps Mr. Mundis can enlighten us about why he didn't provide the origin of that video, which is actually a press conference. There's nothing very special here. Do you have an explanation, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm simply trying to move as expeditiously as possible. All of the information is provided on the table or on the charts which have been provided to the Chamber and to Dr. Seselj. If the Chamber would prefer me to read all this information into the record for each and every one of these tapes, I'm happy to do so, but that of course will mean that we will not finish this exercise today. I'm simply trying to move as expeditiously as possible, in light of the fact that all the information is available to the Judges and to Dr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that it is thanks to my very brief and concise comments that the Prosecutor is proceeding very well today with showing this footage. I did not hold him up in any way. Secondly, you said that we had Natasha Kandic as a source. We haven't had her yet today. This is the first time that we had a tape that she provided. As to all the previous video excerpts, the Prosecutor told us the source, but failed to do so for Natasha Kandic. I didn't say that the Prosecutor wishes to hide this. He informed us in this piece of paper that the source is Natasha Kandic. But this is a public session and he is ashamed to say in public that received it from Natasha Kandic and that he has intense cooperation with her. So that is the crux of the comment I made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall now go on to the next video, the 6062A, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely correct, Mr. President, the next tape bears 65 ter number 6062A. The date of this tape is 18 March 1995. It's clip A from a tape originally broadcast on Srpska Radio Televizija, and this was provided by the embassy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by way of the liaison officer of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Tribunal on 18 March, 1996 in response to a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor dated the 20 February, 1996. This is 65 ter number 6062A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "On the way to Knin and the most western Serbian state, Seselj, president of the Serbian Radical Party, made a call on Prijedor, where several thousand residents of Prijedor greeted him this morning with large applause and acclamation on the plateau in front of the Patria department store. Although somewhat overwhelmed and surprised by such a warm welcome, the popular Vojvoda would not let this take him aback. "'Today we are only passing through heroic Serbian Prijedor on our way to Serbian Krajina, which is currently the most endangered of Serb lands. The future of Serbian Krajina is in the unification -- its unification with Republika Srpska, in the establishment of a single Serbian state, Western Serbia, Western Serbia with its capital in Banja Luka.'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This time, I have a very serious objection to make; that this has been a montage, or the Prosecutor cut this and then gave a segment where I strive for the unification of Krajina with the Republika Srpska. This is the 18th of March, 1995. That's the date of it, and I heard that an aggression was being prepared on the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and I set off from Belgrade for Serbian Krajina and held rallies throughout Serbian Krajina and the unification of its western parts, explaining to the people that an aggression was being prepared and that the Americans and other Western states were behind that aggression. So the Prosecutor cut that part out. Tendentiously I agree that this should be admitted, but I demand that the entire tape be admitted and shown. It wasn't a long speech, it wasn't a planned rally. Suddenly, I was greeted by an overwhelming mass of people, and I made a short speech of maybe 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, do we have the duration of the entire footage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, this again is a compilation tape that was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor. The entire tape runs four hours and five minutes. I'm not sure, sitting here right now, how long Dr. Seselj's speech in Prijedor on this occasion is on that tape, but I will say that this is a clip from a tape that runs more than four hours' long. And, again, let me indicate something that I said a couple of weeks ago, when we were talking about videotapes. You know, on two prior occasions the Office of the Prosecutor has attempted to disclose a number of these tapes on the accused, and he's refused to accept them. As I indicated, I am producing a list. I hope to have it by early next week so that he can select exactly what tapes he wants, and we will again attempt to disclose all of these tapes to him. But I have noticed on several occasions he's indicated that he wants these tapes. We have tried to give him these tapes in the past in digitized electronic form, and he's refused to accept them. So all I can say at this point, Your Honours, is of course Dr. Seselj will be free to show whatever clips he wants during the course of the Defence case. He can show entire clips. He can show as much or as little of this material as he would like. I'll simply leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I believe that last time -- well, he said that he would accept them now. I think that's what he said at the latest time, that he would accept them as long as they were entire -- as long as there was a DVD format so that he could see them. Regarding this video footage, this is very short. It was -- well, it's only a minute long. It's less than a minute long. But we need a number for it. Ms. Registrar, could we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P338, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another objection, Judges, sirs. I rejected DVDs at a time when the OTP was attempting to disclose to me transcripts of witness testimonies of Prosecution witnesses in other cases, collections of documents and so on on DVDs, and then I rejected everything that was on DVD. Now that the Chamber has guaranteed that everything that was on paper has to be disclosed to me on paper and translated into Serbian, I agreed to receive anything that was originally on DVDs, in DVD form. So the Prosecutor should hurry up and disclose all that to me. And, secondly, I wish to point out that every compilation is a manipulation and that the Chamber should reject any compilation whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the more so that you should have the entire footage, notably the tape that's four hours and five minutes' long. Then, you know, once you've seen the entire tape, you can come back to this issue, showing that what the Prosecution is presenting must be scrutinised in light of other elements, which you will be providing during the cross-examination of a Prosecution witness or when you are showing your own witnesses, or leading your own witnesses, or when you testify yourself. But for the moment, everything must be kept as it is. Now, let's move on to another topic, the JCE, joint criminal enterprise. I believe that's what we have on the table. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. The next tape, Your Honours, bears 65 ter number 6013B. This tape is from 7 April 1991. It's clip 1 from a larger tape. This material was received in the Office of the Prosecutor on 28 September 2006. This clip runs a little bit less than eight minutes. It includes a variety of different types of material. This is 65 ter number 6013B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In this sort of atmosphere, Vojvoda Seselj started his speech. "Voja, Voja, Serbia, Serbia, Serbia, Serbia, Serbia. "The Serbian people live here. This is Serbian land, and it will remain Serbian forever. "After labelling the decision on the establishing of the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina, historical Seselj said: 'Serbian brothers and sisters, you find yourselves on the front lines defending the Serbian cause, Serbian state borders. You are in the most difficult position, and you are the pride of the whole of Serbdom. "He has promised them that they will not be left to themselves and that all the Serbs in Croatia have only one party, the Serbian Democratic Party. "'You have a wise and brave leadership here, headed by the heroic Dr. Milan Babic.' "'Those who divide the Serbian people he labelled as traitors. Only Ante Markovic's mercenaries and those of foreign intelligence services believe today that there are more important problems than your defence, your protection. They offer you up to Tudjman. They would sell you. You will not be sold or betrayed.' "Instead of calming them down, Seselj sent a message to the gathered people at the end: "'We are sending a message to the new Ustasha head of state and the Ustasha regime in Croatia. Serbian heads have rolled struck down by the Ustasha hand in the Serbian Krajina. A Serbian head has rolled in Serbian Western Srem and Slavonia as well. We will revenge Serbian blood. We will.' "And when, after Seselj's speech, it seemed that calls to the conquest of Plitvice would not find response, a part of the meetings participants started moving towards the Yugoslav Peoples' Army who had blocked the passage. Despite warnings from the JNA officers that they would not let them pass and that they would use firearms, several thousand participants of the rally passed alongside the tanks heading in the direction of Plitvice."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one observation, after having listened and watched this tape. It would have been interesting to see the crowd moving towards the JNA, and what's going to happen afterwards, and then suddenly it's cut. Just a small detail. Mr. Seselj, it was raining that day and there's a lot of umbrellas out there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the date is wrong here. First of all, it wasn't on the 7th of April, 1991. I'm sure it was on some other day. And, secondly, I think it's scandalous that the footage is cut off here, because in the continuation you can see me going through seven military barricades on the way to Plitvice. I break through some of them with a large mass of people, in spite of well-armed soldiers pointing machine-guns at us, machine-guns where you can see rounds of bullets sticking out, sometimes bypassing them over the hills or over meadows, and all this has been cut out by the Prosecutor. And this is highly significant. In April 1991, and I think it might have been on the 1st or 2nd of May 1991, we were opposed to the JNA. We were in conflict with the JNA. And I think it's very important to show that. You should not permit this. I think you should order the OTP to bring this entire footage here, and then it can be entered into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, when the recording ends, we see the tags. Could we see some extra minutes just to see what's going on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. President, the way this is set up through Sanction, that we would actually have to make another clip of the tape. I'm not sure how long it would take my case manager to do that. It's not very long. Perhaps after the next break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we'll have time to come back to it, anyway, and Mr. Seselj can present this, as long, of course, as he has the entire footage. Personally, there is one thing I would like to note. At that date, we don't know whether it's May or April, but obviously there seems to be an opposition between the one making the speech and the crowd and the army or law and order -- law enforcement forces that are there. We'd have to see the entire footage, anyway. Mr. Seselj, you're not against admitting this excerpt, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am only asking that the entire clip be admitted. Mr. President, the trigger for this was a conflict between the local Serbs and the Croatian special police on the 31st of March, 1991, after which there was a JNA intervention, and the JNA took the Croatian side. The Serbs had to leave Plitvice. Then the Serbs organised a large march towards Plitvice, in spite of the attempts by the JNA to prevent it. The JNA was formerly ostensibly neutral, but it was actually acting on the Croatian side. And I think it's very important to show this from this clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is on the transcript, and the Bench will take into account what you said. Ms. Registrar, could we have a number for this clip.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P339.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 580A. According to our information, this videotape was taken on the 15th of October, 1991. It's about less than 30 seconds' long. This CD, containing documentary film, originated from the BH government and was an exhibit in the Milosevic case. This is 65 ter number 580A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Please, take this seriously. What you are doing is not good. This is the road that you want Bosnia and Herzegovina to take, the same highway of hell and suffering that Slovenia and Croatia have gone through. Don't think you won't take Bosnia and Herzegovina to hell and the Muslim people to possible extinction."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's scandalous that only 23 seconds of this footage has been shown. It's evident that Dr. Radovan Karadzic is warning the Muslim political leadership not to one-sidedly declare the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He's warning them that this cannot be done without a war. We have to see this through a more complete fragment. I'm not asking for the entire speech now, but for a more extended clip. Karadzic is acting with good intentions here, not with malicious intentions. This is evidently -- this 1991, before there was any sort of war in Bosnia, October 1991. There was no war between the Serbs and Muslims in Bosnia at that time. This was before independence was declared. And I explained to you in my opening statement that no one could declare the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina without one of the constituent nations. Any manipulation with footage is falsifying the footage. If you cut off the footage in a most inconvenient place, you're actually falsifying the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What you have said is on the transcript. You're telling us that when he's talking, Dr. Karadzic is talking in a certain direction, and we shouldn't misread what he is saying. According to you, if we looked at the entire footage, we would have the real meaning. In passing, I could say that this might be established when Mr. Karadzic will be heard as a witness and when we hear him in this Tribunal. It's not in despair. Maybe we'll have enough time to find him. Now, this being said, these 30 seconds will be admitted, and we need a number. Of course, this cassette must be seen again at one point in time. I'm sure Mr. Seselj will be able to have this cassette shown, maybe when he has Mr. Karadzic as a witness. Mr. Seselj, you want to take the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm convinced that no one will ever catch Dr. Radovan Karadzic. I'm absolutely sure of that. But I might call him as a Defence witness in these proceedings. Before that, he would have to have safe passage, a guarantee that he can come here freely, testify, and then go back to where he came from. Under such conditions, I would call him here as a Defence witness, both Dr. Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic, and Hadzic and Stojan Stupljin [phoen]. I know where they are. I can reach them easily, but I don't want to until you grant them safe passage. I would sacrifice my life for them never to be brought here in handcuffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not going to ask him where they are, because I'm not sure he would tell us. Let's give a number, please. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber agrees with Mr. Seselj. We would need to have a more comprehensive view of the footage to know what was said beforehand and after. Thirty seconds is a bit short to assess anything. However, we will give it an MFI number. Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P340 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not sure what time the Chamber was anticipating the next recess. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have the break now, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps before we proceed to the next clip, I do have now, and I would ask with the assistance of the usher, I have the 12 DVDs containing all of the videos that are on the Prosecution 65 ter list, and I would just at this point ask that these be provided, along with two copies of the receipt, to the accused, Dr. Seselj, so we at least have eliminated the disclosure of those videotapes, and we can clear that off the radar screen for the foreseeable future. If I'm not mistaken, Mr. President, we will adjourn this evening at 1830. Is that correct? I do have a couple of other issues that I would ask to address the Chamber on at the end of the videotapes, so I would propose what we do is complete the current theme, if you will, and then skip the rather large number of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Usher, could you please get the receipt from the accused, to give it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, I would propose that we complete the videos in the current theme and then, in effect, skip the section on instigation, hate speech and propaganda for a later day. We could then continue with the two smaller themes that contain a smaller number of videotapes, because as I indicated, I have a couple of other issues that need to be raised before we adjourn for the week. So what I would do is play these sections and then skip the theme on instigation, hate speech and propaganda, save those tapes for another day, and then skip to the remaining two or three themes that only have a small number of videos, which should allow us to finish by 1830 today, if that's okay with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next clip bears 65 ter number 1836B, 1836B. This is clip E from a tape that was originally broadcast on Serbian Television. This tape was received in 1998 from an unknown source. At the end of this programme, the date 15 May 1993 appears. This is 65 ter number 1836B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mr. Milosevic, in his last conversation with journalists, one which was broadcast on television, stated that no one can dispute the existence of Republika Srpska. "Yes, but this is the first time he has said something like that. He never made such statements before. And if you remember after the Vance-Owen Plan, they stopped even using the term 'Republika Srpska' on news broadcasts. Instead, they used the Serbian side in Bosnia, the Muslim side, the Croatian side, and that went on for a few months. Now they are come back to that because they have the pre-election propaganda need to prove themselves as nationalists, as true Serbian patriots. "Tell me, these people who were arrested in the last couple of days for possession -- illegal possession, that is, of weapons and for some other acts for which a reasonable doubt exists, there are grounds for suspect, do they belong to your party? "Some of them belong to the Serbian Radical Party, but most of them are not our members. Milenko Petric, for example, is one of our members, and he received an automatic gun with a receipt from the government, from the police at the time when the Serbs living in border region of Srem, Sandzak, and Kosovo Metohija were being armed. He got it with a receipt, and now they arrested him because of it, and they arrested some other people who got this with a receipt from the state at the time of arming. "Then they arrested Gradimir Milosevic in Sremska Mitrovica in whose possession no weapons were found. And they also arrested some other members of ours, and most of them are not our members but are put into the same pot. And they are showing a lot of weapons, but I would not be surprised to find out these are the same weapons they show when they arrest Albanian terrorists, when they arrest Muslim terrorists from Sandzak and so on. On one recording you could even see a stamp with a Croatian coat of arms. This is the best evidence of what sort of framing is going on. You can clearly see the 'sahovnica,' the Croatian checkerboard coat of arms."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This can in no way be dated the 15th of May, 1993. This must have been filmed sometime in October 1993, when there was already a vehement conflict between the Serbian Radical Party and Milosevic's regime. And the police started arresting members of the Serbian Radical Party and other people, not only members, on whom they found a certain weapon. And then Milosevic's party started a campaign against the Serbian Radical Party. The most unscrupulous means were used in that campaign. We were accused of being criminals. I was said to be an alcoholic and so on. They did not choose their means. Anyone who was arrested in October was soon released. Their arrest was only for the purposes of the election campaign, because the Serbian Radical Party set out to topple Milosevic's government. Milosevic disbanded the National Assembly, and so elections were about to be held. So this must have been in November or October of 1993. It cannot be in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Given these observations you made, you seem to say that this video must be dated in October, not in May. It needs a number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And one more thing, Mr. President. You know that the indictment is limited. The relevant time is limited to the beginning of the conflict between the Serbian Radical Party and myself, personally, with the regime of Slobodan Milosevic, and that's September 1993. So the question of relevance arises, the issue of temporal relevance. But that's not so much at issue. What matters is the correct date be given to the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, just to give you my opinion on relevance. There is relevance because there is mention of weapons that would have been given by the JNA with receipts. Having heard this, I think I understand that when volunteers were given weapons, they had to sign some kind of form, some kind of receipt. So this could be very interesting, to have this evidence, even if it is outside the period of reference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say this has never been mentioned here before, but this is not just about volunteers, but also the arming of the population in the border belts and in flash-points; for example, in the west of Srem, in B acka, where the Croats infiltrated sabotage groups, some of these groups were arrested. The local population was issued with weapons and the receipts written for these weapons, and it was for them to defend themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you for this. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next clip bears 65 ter number 6059A. This tape apparently is from sometime in 1994. This clip runs a little bit less than one minute. It was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by a protected witness. We received this tape on or about 1 May 1996. This is 65 ter number 6059A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "You said on television yesterday that in the past he was the one who actually gave weapons to your volunteers and took an active part in this, and then he turned his back on everything. What's that? "Yes, that's a fact. Milosevic was pursuing a prominently patriotic and nationalistic policy in 1991 and 1992, and we had maximal cooperation at the time. We sent almost 30.000 volunteers to all the battlefields where the Serbian people were fighting in this war, and Slobodan Milosevic equipped us with weapons, ammunition, military uniforms, he put a barracks in Bubanj Potok at our disposal, provided transportation to battlefields and so on."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Evidently nobody knows when this interview was filmed and on what occasion. But at the beginning, we had an insert from a courtroom. I think this is the trial in Sabac of members of the Yellow Wasps. These two things are linked here in an illogical manner. I explained this in public more than once. This attack on Milosevic is, in fact, a personification of the regime. So when I say "Milosevic," I'm referring to the whole regime. Milosevic was the center we were striking at. Whatever the regime had done, we said Milosevic had done it. The figure of 30.000 volunteers is exaggerated. I was exaggerating this for propaganda purposes. However, the expert who knows nothing, says there were only about a thousand. The realistic figure would be 10.000. For reasons of propaganda, we blew this figure up a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's give this a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P342, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next clip bears 65 ter number 2068A, 2068A. This clip apparently is from 13 August 1994. It runs two minutes 45 seconds' long. It was received from AID Sarajevo on or about 20 May 1999. This is 65 ter number 2068A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The president of Republika Srpska and speaker of the Republican Serbian Assembly, Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik, and Krajisnik met this evening in Republic Presidency with the Serbian Radical Party delegation headed by Dr. Seselj. After their talks and their address to the press, Seselj and Karadzic emphasised the following: "The top-level delegation of the Serbian Radical Party is visiting Republika Srpska. We came here to express our solidarity between the Serbian Radical Party and our brothers this side of the Drina at this crucial moment in their fight for freedom. The Serbian Radical Party strictly condemns the blockade imposed by the regime in Belgrade against Republika Srpska, and we're going to do everything in our power to lift this blockade as soon as possible. This blockade is by far more severe and harsh than the one imposed on Serbia and Montenegro and therefore it has to be lifted sooner, let alone its inhumanness, lack of morals, let alone that nothing similar has ever been recorded in the history of the Serbian people. The Serbian Radical Party has always been supporting the fight of our brothers this side of the Drina River, Serbs from Republika Srpska, and we feel that their fight will soon be victorious and that the Serbian cause will triumph, regardless of all the problems and difficulties and temptations the great powers put before us and lately even the regime in Belgrade. "The Serbian Radical Party has always supported the leadership of Republika Srpska because we respect their patriotism and dedication in the service of their people. "It is our pleasure to have had a top-level delegation of the Serbian Radical party visiting us. This is precious to us, especially in view of the situation we are in at the moment. It is precious from the viewpoint of preserving total unity of the Serbian people. It is precious from the aspect of the support we have, which is more precious at this moment than it would be in peace time or in any neutral situation. We have always had good relations, and more importantly we have never been in a position to fight for power. Even if that would be the case, it seems to me that we would never sacrifice national interests to a mere power struggle. I will repeat that every vote, those in Serbia who understands us, is particularly precious to us, especially if it's a parliamentary or influential party, and in that regard we're happy that this visit came about, and some other parties have announced their visits to show their solidarity. "The radical Party of Serbia also express their support to the people of Republika Srpska and their leadership."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objections to make. I'm proud of this tape and grateful to the Prosecution for digging it up, because I haven't got it in my possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit P343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last video in the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. This tape bears ERN -- excuse me, 65 ter number 6068A. The date of this tape is 13 March 1995. It originally was broadcast on Srpska Radio-Televizija. This clip runs a little bit less than 3 minutes'. It was received by the Office of the Prosecutor on 20 October 1995 from the liaison officer of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mrs. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "It is much harder for us to send volunteers now than it was in 1991, 1992, or 1993. When we sent volunteers at that time, we had good cooperation with Slobodan Milosevic. He would give us uniforms, weapons, buses. He granted the entire barracks at Bubanj Potok. He put it at the disposal of the Serbian Radical Party and all the technical equipment that we needed, and this functioned much better. Because of treason committed by Slobodan Milosevic, the Serbian Radical Party now faces huge difficulties when sending and equipping volunteers. Our volunteers now have to leave wearing civilians clothes to areas where they're called by some commands of the Serbian Krajina, mostly the western part of Serbian Krajina, where the population is scarce and where our assistance is most needed. These volunteers travel by buses through the corridor via Banja Luka and so on, and the Serbs there know about this. We can't speak of any numbers, but it's much harder for us to provide buses now, for example, and basic equipment for the volunteers. "The volunteers are given weapons in the places where they arrive, and they are given uniforms, and footwear, and everything else they need, and our situation is all the more complicated, and the process of preparing volunteers takes more time. But in spite of this, we're able to send as much volunteers as the Command of the Serbian Army requests at any one time."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question of relevance arises here. If the Prosecution wished to prove that I stated something like this on the 13th of March, 1995, then the Prosecutor has proved that, because I really did state that. But what is the purpose of it all, where's the relevance? If the Prosecution wishes to show the truthfulness of these words and that they were suited to the occasion, they're not able to do so, because this is a political appearance where the entire regime is personified in Belgrade and equated to Milosevic, in his name. And the Prosecution has shown a lot of evidence and will have many witnesses at its disposal, and everybody in the OTP knows how the volunteers were armed, how they received their uniforms, who they received them from. It's no secret. At this point in time, it was still a secret, the barracks at Bubanj Potok, the way in which cooperation with the JNA evolved and so on, and then personifying the attack on Milosevic for blockading Republika Srpska, for instance, and for not allowing a passage across the Drina River and because the blockade took on more intensive forms, and so on and so forth. We come to the question of what the Prosecution wishes to prove here. If they wish to prove that I stated this, then it's done that. If it wishes to prove the conflict with Milosevic, it has done that. Now, if this is prove and evidence about the way in which the volunteers were armed, equipped and prepared, then this is no proof whatsoever because it is in collision with the other evidence and exhibits -- material evidence that the Prosecution disposes of, the papers relating to arming, equipping, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the Prosecutor will later on say to us what he is attempting to prove in this way, and this will no doubt appear in his last brief or during the questioning of future witnesses. Let's give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P344.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point we would propose skipping the next chapter entitled "Instigation, Hate Speech, and Propaganda," moving approximately four or five pages ahead to the section entitled "Recruitment and Location of Volunteers." The next clip is 65 ter number 6015B. This is from May 1991. It is a clip from a programme entitled "Without Incisions and Without Anesthesia," from TV Novi Sad. The clip runs approximately one minute and 35 seconds. This tape was received from AID Sarajevo on 27 August 1998. This is 65 ter number 6015B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "You said modestly within the framework of our capabilities and limits. What is the Serbian Radical Party and Chetnik Movement doing in terms of concrete action to help the Serbs? "Well, the Serbian Chetnik movement organises the sending of volunteers, Serbian Chetniks, where the Serbs are in jeopardy. We've already sent a lot of Serbian volunteers, Chetniks, to various parts of Western Serbian lands in Slavonia, Baranja, Western Srem, and Dalmatia, Lika, Banja, and Kordun."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know why this is so brief, just a few seconds. I don't mind it being admitted into evidence, but I think it should have been a more extensive excerpt. I would like to draw your attention to the fact that it is outside the period relevant to the indictment. It is May 1991. And here we see a persistent tendency on the part of the OTP, on the part of the Prosecution, to equate the state of the volunteers from April, May, and June 1991, and then from July and August 1991, and then from September 1991 onwards when the cooperation was established with the JNA. It was done in one way when it was only the Serbian Radical Party that was engaged in this. It was different when various parties pooled their efforts with the Association of Serbs in Croatia, that was in the summer of 1991, and it was done in a third way when cooperation with the JNA was established. So I have the impression that this is intentionally misleading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So that has been taken note of. You have called the attention of the Chamber on several occasions to the importance of the dates, and what we see, volunteers. Let's give this document a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P345.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip on the list, Your Honours, is 65 ter number 6045A, 6045A, from 27 July 1991. This clip runs approximately 70 seconds, is from RTS, and was submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor on 25 October 2002. This is 6045A.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Dr. Vojislav Seselj, president of the Serbian Radical Party, visited Borovo Selo today. "The Serbian people located in the most dangerous areas have to persevere. They must show patience and will because they bear the heavy burden. Most things depend on their strength, courage, and determination. "Are the units of your party ready to help at this moment? "We have no party units. What we do is to organise the registration of volunteers in Serbia and send them where they're needed, and they appear in villages where they're being asked to come by Serb villagers, and they immediately join up with the local units under the command of the village staffs. So we have no special units in the region, nor is there any need for them. We'll all Serbs today, regardless of our party affiliation. I don't recognize any party divisions until the borders of Serbia are secured. "Vojislav Seselj, president of the Serbian Radical Party, met with Vladika, the orthodox bishop Lukijan from the area of Osijek-Polje, who said that all Serbs must be unanimous and united, because that is in their best interest."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P346, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next clip bears 65 ter number 6062B, 6062B. The date of this tape is 20 March 1995. This clip comes from Serbian Radio-TV. It runs approximately one and a half minutes 'long. This was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor on 18 March 1996 by the liaison officer of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Vasvija Vidovic, pursuant to a request for assistance dated 20 February 1996. This is 6062B.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Vid Vukelic from Banja Luka, local Commune of Laos, asks whether and how far are the radicals ready to help their brothers on this side of the Drina River in the case of a major enemy offensive. "We are ready at any time we're needed and are able to send a certain number of volunteers. Even now, we have several groups active in the territory of Republika Srpska. At Majevica, Manda Maksimovic has been there since the beginning of the war, Slavko Aleksic, also a Vojvoda, at the Jewish cemetery at Sarajevo. One group is in Herzegovina, Vojvoda Nedeljko was killed there recently. We also sent groups of fighters according to need to Srebrenica, Olovo and Vogosca. We have one group with Vojvoda Vesko in Cekrcici from the first day of the war near Ilijas and so on. The moment they're needed, we will send them again. "This time, it will be much more difficult than before. Before, we had the weapons and uniforms and buses of Slobodan Milosevic and his regime and the barracks in Bubanj Potok. This time our people will come to go in civilian clothes, but this time too we will send as many volunteers as needed and wherever needed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My objection is this: The tape is not an integral one. If we were played the whole tape, then you would see the whole situation. I say where we sent volunteers and where we had volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party, but I enumerated the places where we had volunteers, not ones sent from Serbia, but the local ones, Mita Macevic [phoen], Manda Majevica [phoen], for instance, Vasvija Vidovic in Cerkrici near Ilijas, Slavko Aleksic at the Jewish cemetery in Sarajevo and so on and so forth. So one should differentiate between the two. I am saying where we sent them, to Srebrenica, but that was not in 1995. It was in 1992 and 1993 when the Muslims from Srebrenica broke through into the surrounding Serbian villages and slaughtered the people, burnt them and so on. In January 1993, that was. We sent two groups to Skelani to liberate Serbian villages, and a group of Serb soldiers were under siege in the village of Jezero, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's give this document a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there's still one more to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. This tape is 65 ter number 1808A, 1808A, taken on 17 March 1993. This clip runs about four minutes' long from ITN. It was seized on 17 February 2003 and provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by Andres J. Redelmeier. This is 1808A.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: "The people of Bijeljina gather in the town's main square to bask in the first springs sunshine. Their enjoyment is marred by the noise of bulldozers. "They're levelling the site where the town's main mosque used to stand. It was still there last Friday night. Now there's nothing left. "These pictures were taken from a moving car because we were strictly forbidden from filming the demolished mosque site. We were not even allowed to get close to where the town's four mosques stood. They were also destroyed in the early hours of last Saturday. "This is what the main square used to look like. The mosque a prominent feature of the multi-ethnic town. That chapter of the" --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We must stop there, Mr. President, we must interrupt this, because I'm not receiving any interpretation whatsoever. At the beginning, the interpreter just said, making a voiceover, that they didn't have the transcript, so this cannot be shown until the transcript is provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's start over again and ask the interpreters to translate for Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: "REPORTER: The people of Bijeljina gather in the town's main square to bask in the first springs' sunshine. Their enjoyment is marred by the noise of bulldozers. "They're levelling the site where the town's main mosque used to stand. It was still there last Friday night. Now there's nothing left. "These pictures were taken from a moving car because we were strictly forbidden from filming the demolished mosque site. We were not even allowed to get close to where the town's four mosques stood. They were also destroyed in the early hours of last Saturday. "This is what the main square used to look like. The mosque a prominent feature of the multi-ethnic town. That chapter of Bijeljina history has been wiped out. "Two hours before the mosques were blown up, full telephone lines form Bijeljina were cut. Bulldozers had to finish the demolition job at this mosque because it was only partially blown up to spare surrounding buildings. It is allegedly the work of an extreme Serb nationalist militia we encountered on the streets called 'The Panthers.' Their commander, not seen here, is called Ljubisa Savic, but is known as Major Mouser [phoen]. He wants all the Muslims out of Bijeljina by April 15th. "The Serbian mayor of Bijeljina apparently knew beforehand and opposed the plans to destroy the mosques. With the sound of bulldozers behind him, he talks of his helplessness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "It is my ... "REPORTER: My feelings about this are ones of sorrow and sadness and I'm trying to come to terms with it because I think this act will do nobody any good, least of all the Serbian people. We've always lived with the Muslim population quite normally. "The sound of gunfire is often heard on the streets of Bijeljina, and people pretend not to notice. There's been no fighting in the town since last May. The firing from the guns of the paramilitaries is purely to create fear among Muslims. Of some 15.000 Muslims who originally lived here, around 4.000 remain. "And many of those are now leaving too. These Muslim families are bound for Vienna. The armed militia men who put them on these coaches out of sight of our cameras say these people are leaving voluntarily and it's true that they want to go to flee. They're too afraid to say they've been driven out by acts such as the destruction of the mosques. "This old man was one of the few Muslims willing to risk being seen talking to us. 'This lady was not born in Serbia. She's not Serbian, only Bosnian. A Bosnian Orthodox, but not Serb. I am Muslim. But I'm not Arabian or Turkish. I'm a Bosnian Muslim. This man is a Catholic, not from Rome or Germany but a Bosnian Catholic. And what now? Somebody forced us to hate each other and is still forcing it.' "We left the man outside the local Red Cross office where families divided by war try to contact each other. This Serbian's woman's older son is off fighting somewhere on the front line. She thinks her husband is still at their home in Muslim held territory. "'If I could only hear the voice of my child. I want to know if they're alive or not. They had to surrender because they were the minority. I know it's asking for so much to put us in touch for each other, I would even pay for it, just to know that they're still alive.' "Most local Serbs appeared shocked by what had happened to the mosques. "'This is just propaganda to get us to fight each other. Everybody is against it. The army officer said that asking each other who is responsible, someone who really wants Serbs and Muslim people to fight. I was in church today and the priest was crying, saying how sorry he was, asking What's happening to us.'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this videotape is absolutely irrelevant, and I oppose to it being admitted into evidence for the following reasons: This happened in 1993. The mosque was destroyed in Bijeljina. That is an indisputable fact, and that's one year after the liberation of Bijeljina. On the tape, it is stated that the mosque was destroyed by a paramilitary unit called "The Panthers." Now, the Prosecution has a large number of documents and evidence from which we're able to see that the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian Chetnik Movement, in Bijeljina, were constantly in a severe conflict with this paramilitary formation called "Panther," and that they publicly attacked it for the persecution of the Muslim population. The Prosecution has that. Now, the Command of that Panthers military unit was Ljubisa Savic, nicknamed Mouser, and later on he was the vice-president of the Democratic Party in Serbia, vice-president to Zoran Djindjic and the president of that party in Republika Srpska when Djindjic decided that the Democratic Party from Serbia should expand to include the territory of Republika Srpska and to be in competition there to Karadzic's Democratic Party, a rival to it. The Prosecutor can show you those documents from which you can see this constant clash between the Serb radicals and Mouser and his paramilitary units. Now whether this is truthful or not, whether he really did destroy the mosque, I can't say. I don't actually know who destroyed it. But on this tape, it says that this was done by the Panthers, the paramilitary formation, and it has absolutely nothing to do with the Serbian Radical Party, no connection between the Serbian Radical Party and the Panthers. There never, ever was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask my fellow Judges what their position is, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. After having deliberated, the Bench believes that it would be appropriate to admit this video into the evidence, and we shall attribute a number to it as a consequence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P348.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, you can keep on standby the other videos that you will be able to show us when we will have an opportunity to do so. For instance, if witnesses don't come along, we can use them to fill in the extra time. Let me give you the floor for the other issues you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and we will also be reviewing other video material, perhaps supplementing the list of material that was left over from today, and of course we'll be providing that list in both English and Serbian in due course. I wanted to address two or perhaps three issues briefly. The first had to do with the issue regarding the disclosure of transcripts of the testimony of Witness VS-51. Two days ago, the accused raised the issue concerning disclosure of the transcripts of this witness, and based upon our information, contrary to what he has stated, he has received full disclosure of the transcripts of the testimony of this witness. I believe there is perhaps some misunderstanding about what exactly is available and what was, in fact, disclosed. It would appear that the accused has alleged that upon review of the transcript, it appeared to him that the witness had testified on 15 February 2006. I don't know what the basis for that belief is. Clearly, based on the transcripts of the prior trial, the witness began his testimony on 16 February 2006, as reflected of page 4477 of the English transcripts. I do have a copy of that, if that would be of assistance to anyone. The witness finished his testimony on the 22nd of February, 2006, which is readily apparent from the fact that the transcript of the hearing the following day, the 23rd of February, 2006, at page 4863, clearly indicates that a new witness is taking the oath and beginning his testimony. Secondly, Your Honours will recall --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, let's deal with matters one at a time, Mr. President, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, go ahead. Mr. Seselj, what can you say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Looking at the transcript during the weekend, I've read through everything that was supplied to me, the transcript begins on the 17th of February, as far as I know from what I received, and in the text, on page 1, somebody is saying to the witness, perhaps the lawyer asking the question says, "Yesterday, you said such-and-such," or the Prosecutor is continuing with the interview. I can't remember. Perhaps Mr. Mundis has it in front of him. But, anyway, on page 1 of what I received, it says that there was something that happened the previous day, on the 16th, whereas I have the transcript of the 17th. And on the last page, which is the 22nd of February, the last page that I received, it says that there was a pause, a break, and that things would continue at 1605 hours in the evening. So the break was at a quarter to 6.00, and like now, five past 6.00, there was a continuation, but I don't have the continuation. Perhaps they got together at 6.15 and somebody said, "We're going to finish there and not conduct the interview further," but maybe they did go on working, maybe for five minutes or 55 minutes. That's the portion I'm lacking. You see, I remember everything quite precisely, although it was last weekend. So if page 1 is the 17th of February, you can read what it says there and you'll see that somebody is asking the witness what he said on the previous day, which would be the 16th. You have that in front of you. And if the last page is the 22nd of February, see when the break was announced and when the continuation at 1605 hours took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will put here on the record the fact that the witness testified on five days; 16 February 2006, 17 February 2006, 20 February 2006, 21 February 2006, and 22 February 2006. Those are the days of his testimony. The disclosure receipt number 202 indicates that we have disclosed to the accused the transcripts both on the 13th of February, 2008 -- sorry, the 16th of February, 2006, and on the 4th of December, 2007. So these transcripts from these five days have been previously disclosed on the 16th of February, 2006, with respect to certain days, and again on the 4th of December, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, Mr. Seselj is saying that he was looking at the transcript, the transcript of the 17th of February. He noted that somebody said, "Yesterday, you ... " this or that, so "yesterday" would mean the 16th of February. And Mr. Seselj is saying there must be a transcript for February 16, and Mr. Seselj is telling us that he only obtained the 17th of February and not the 16th of February. I don't have the page of February 17th in front of me, but that's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I certainly did not receive the transcript of the 16th of February, and Mr. Mundis can check and see whether they have it translated in the OTP. So why haven't I been provided with the 16th of February one? My transcript begins with the 17th of February and ends with the 22nd, up until the break. Now, I don't know what happened after the break at 1805 hours. That's where it ends, as far as I'm concerned. That's all I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will check again with respect to the transcript on the 22nd of February, 2006. But according to our records, on the 13th of February, 2008, receipt number 202, the transcripts of the witness on the 16th of February, 2006, were disclosed. So there is a transcript from 16 February 2006, and it was disclosed to the accused on the 13th of February of this year under receipt number 202. And I will double-check the transcripts from the 22nd of February, 2006, to determine if there was, in fact, anything that happened after the break, the last break of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Mr. Mundis is telling us that the transcript for February 16th was disclosed to you, and that corresponds to receipt 202.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there's only one receipt. The prison guards bring me what the OTP sends me. It may be ten different documents, and I don't count the pages of each and every document I receive. I sign for everything I receive from the OTP twice, a receipt for the prison administration, the registry, and one for the OTP. I receive this in good faith. I don't count the pages. However, once I started working on this material, and that was last weekend, I saw that the transcript of the 16th of February was missing. Let's make an experiment. Let Mr. Mundis show you that there is a transcript of the 16th of February in Serbian, and then he will be more right than I am, but I don't have it in Serbian, the one of the 16th. And I stated on time that I didn't have it. I stated on Tuesday last week that I didn't have it, and the witness was due to appear the following week. So I wasn't trying to throw a spanner in the works of the OTP. I was simply stating that I did not have this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, do you have the transcript of February 16th in B/C/S? If you do, please give it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, we do have it. I'll print it right now. I don't have it in hard copy, sitting here. We'll print it out right now, and it will be provided immediately. And perhaps while I'm on my feet with the next topic, my case manager can also check the 22nd and see if there's anything after 1800 on that day concerning the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 22nd of February, after 1805 onwards, that's what I'm missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Bench may break at 6.00 p.m. -- either if they were going to resume at 6.05 or if they made a break at 6.00, there should be something -- there should be an end to the transcript, unless they decided to make a break and not resume the hearing. That might be. So for February 22nd, the last page of the transcript, all pages have a number, so the last page of the transcript must show some trace of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're checking, and I have just now been handed the signed receipt 202 that makes reference to disclosure of the transcripts of 16 February 2006. I'm happy to provide this both to the Chamber or to the accused, if he'd like to see it, but I do have a signed receipt dated the 13th of February of this year, indicating that we disclosed the transcripts from the 16th of February. But as I said, I've asked that they be printed out again, and they're on their way down here as I speak. And we're checking the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In this document, it states very clearly that there was February 16, then 17, 21, and 22nd. If he signs, maybe he didn't check immediately that the 16th was actually included. And then later on, when he looked at it, he noticed that he had the 17th, the 20th, the 21st, and the 22nd, and that the 16th was missing. That might have happened. There might have been an error in the transfer and disclosure, you thought it was included in the series and it wasn't. That's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At any rate, Mr. President, the transcript is being printed and is, hopefully, going to appear like magic within the next few minutes. Let me turn, then, to the issue of the 22nd of February, 2006. As reflected on page 4844 of the Sljivancanin trial, at the top of the page Judge Parker basically tells -- I don't want to name the name of the witness, but Judge Parker says -- speaking to the witness: "Would you please go with the Court Officer and we will hear what counsel have to say. We will then have a break, and if you are wanted again, you will be advised and will come in after the break. Thank you." The witness withdrew from the courtroom. There were then some submissions by counsel. A recess was then taken at 17 hours 47 minutes. The hearing then, as reflected on the transcript on page 4853, indicates the hearing resumed at 18 hours 9 minutes. The witness was not brought back into the courtroom. There is no further testimony of the witness after the break, and then the hearing adjourned after, again, some further submissions by counsel in that case. So the testimony of the witness, based upon what is reflected in the transcript, was not recalled after the final recess or break on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That page, Mr. President, that page, where you can see that the witness's testimony did not continue after 6.05 or 1805, I didn't receive that, so I didn't know whether the witness had continued testifying after that time or not. That page is missing from what I received. The Prosecutor might have said that at once. It did not continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I believe that the best solution is to print out the last page, the one that you have just read out, and disclose it to Mr. Seselj in his own language. That way he will understand that the Trial Chamber asked the witness to leave the courtroom, telling him, "We'll listen to your counsel, and if we need -- we'll listen to counsel, and if need be, you'll come back." They listened to the submissions, they had the break, and then they found out that they didn't need the witness back, and so the witness never came back in the courtroom. They moved on to another topic. I believe that this is what is -- that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I even have the procedural discussion by the counsel. I have everything up to the break which was declared, and the hearing was to resume at 1805. I have the debate. I think the Prosecutor was involved as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, after 6.05, when the hearing resumed, there must be a trace of the topics that were dealt with, and the hearing must have been adjourned at 7.00 p.m. So this last page does exist. It can be printed and given to Mr. Seselj, and that way he will see, you know, the witness never came back into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: They resumed at 1809, not 1805, and the transcripts continue for approximately ten pages, where counsel are discussing a number of procedural matters. I will -- we do not have that translated into Serbian. I will put that into the pipeline, but of course that means other priorities will have to be pushed off, number 1, or, number 2, this will go to the end of the queue and it will be many, many months before this transcript might be made available.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I have to interrupt Mr. Mundis and cut this short. It suffices for me that Mr. Mundis told me orally that the witness did not reappear in the courtroom, so let me just get the 16th of February document that Mr. Mundis says has been translated, and then that makes it simple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Seselj is trusting you. He believes that the witness did not come back after 6.05, at 6.09, when the hearing resumed. All he wants is a transcript for February 16th. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The next issue concerns the schedule for next week. Perhaps out of an abundance of caution, we should perhaps go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, I say this: We will resume on Tuesday. The legal officer will tell the Prosecution and Mr. Seselj the time that we have set aside for procedural matters. That way, everybody will know what is scheduled for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of April, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.45 p.m.,
